pr_body:
Today this test suite relies on being able to cancel an in-flight
publication after it's reached a committed state. This is questionable,
and also a little flaky in the presence of the desired balance allocator
which may introduce a short delay before enqueuing the cluster state
update that performs the reconciliation step.

This commit removes the questionable meddling with the internals of
`Coordinator` and instead just blocks the cluster state updates at the
transport layer to achieve the same effect.

Closes #102947

review_comments: When can the data node have a cluster state version higher than master's?

We technically can't guarantee the absence of any background process which might perform another cluster state update after `finalClusterStateVersion`. But the point is we don't care about any such process, we just want to confirm that the data node processes a cluster state that is at least as new as `finalClusterStateVersion`.
ah, sorry, I missed that we record the version of the master's CS outside the `assertBusy`.
I think the setup of this test could also simplified by using a master-only node.
Yeah I just didn't want to change the overall flow of these tests too much.
but it would be much simpler and kind of a small change, wouldn't it?
Not obviously much simpler, but maybe a little easier to follow - see dc6bfb204be.
Why do we need this special trivial update? Can't we e.g. just add a mapping to the index or something similar that causes a new CS?
We could, any cluster state update would do, but something meaningful like a mapping update would potentially interfere with the whole point of the test.
I guess we could instead wait to see the matching state in the requestHandlingbehavour? I'm not asking for this, but wondering if that would be the alternative to the sleep.

The sleep itself is kind of optional, we know there's enough jitter in the scheduling of these things in CI that we end up seeing concurrency issues even without carefully-crafted sleeps like this one. I don't think it's sufficient to wait on anything in the requestHandlingbehavour tho, that'd tell us that we've rejected a cluster state update but not really anything about whether the indexing operation has been processed or not.
